What I learned from writing every day for a year

Small habits beat big plans, even when nobody is reading.

Maya Lindqvist
6 min read · Sep 14, 2026

Last September I promised myself that I would write something every single day. Not a masterpiece, just a few honest paragraphs.

The first week was exciting. The second week was painful. By the third week, it had simply become part of the morning.

Lesson one: lower the bar

On bad days I allowed myself to write a single sentence. Surprisingly, a single sentence usually turned into a page.

You don't need more time. You need a smaller first step.

Lesson two: publish before you are ready

Sharing unfinished work felt uncomfortable, but the feedback made the next piece much better.
